covers: The eight registers of the SN76496 family, named by the register field of a latch byte

entries.name: tone 0 period
entries.description: Channel 0's tone period: the 10-bit count its generator reloads, so a low value is a high pitch.
entries.behaviour: A latch byte (1 00 0 dddd) sets the low four bits and a following data byte the high six. Period 0 is taken as 0x400 except on the Sega chips, where it stays 0.
entries.differs: DOSBox-X's test is the other way round: it takes period 0 as 0 except on the Sega chips, where it becomes 0x400.

sources.ref: datasheet:SMS Power! SN76489 development page, https://www.smspower.org/Development/SN76489, SN76489 registers
sources.cites: Tone registersThese give a counter reset value for the tone generators. Hence, low values give high frequencies and vice versa.

entries.name: tone 0 attenuation
entries.description: Tone 0's attenuation: 0 is full volume and 15 is silence, in 2 dB steps.
entries.behaviour: A latch byte (1 00 1 dddd) sets the 4-bit attenuation. Level 15 is off.
entries.differs: DOSBox-X's NCR8496 ignores a data byte (bit 7 clear) for this register; MAME has that rule commented out until verified on hardware.

sources.cites: Volume registersThe value represents the attenuation of the output. Hence, %0000 is full volume and %1111 is silence.

entries.name: noise control
entries.description: The noise channel's mode and shift rate.
entries.behaviour: Bits 1 and 0 select the shift rate (N/512, N/1024, N/2048, or tone 2's output) and bit 2 white noise (1) or periodic noise (0). A write resets the noise shift register, on the NCR8496 only when bit 2 changes.
entries.differs: DOSBox-X's NCR8496 ignores a data byte (bit 7 clear) for this register; MAME has that rule commented out until verified on hardware.

sources.cites: Noise registerOne bit selects the mode ("periodic" or "white") and the other two select a shift rate.
